title: The importance of frameworks for building confidence in toxicological new approach methods
content: For more than two decades, the scientific community has focused considerable effort on developing New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) capable of informing chemical or drug toxicity while reducing animal testing. These efforts have encompassed both the development of fit-for-purpose alternatives to traditional studies and the creation of mechanistic tools designed to address toxicological endpoints that have historically proven difficult to evaluate, such as developmental neurotoxicity and endocrine disruption. During the acceleration phase of NAMs research, discussions largely centered on method development and predictive capacity. Today, the conversation is entering a new phase in which NAMs are increasingly being evaluated for integration into toxicology testing strategies and assessment frameworks. This transition moves the field beyond method development toward establishing the scientific confidence required for informed decision-making.
